title: The harness seam carries both activation shapes and the orchestrator carries none
requirement: REQ-296: the harness seam is the only owner of the two subagent activation shapes. C01: plugins/orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs contains no activation-form fields (no spec.request, maxDepth, outputSchema or ...request) and calls the seam. C02: one input yields both forms, each read by its own reader; the form is chosen by name and an unknown form is an explicit refusal, not a silent fallback. C03: docs/HARNESS-CONTRACT.md lists the calls with their owner and check.
steps: Build one delegation input (role, preset, prompt, parent) and call activationSpec with the default form: read spec.request.parent.id and spec.parent.id.
Call activationSpec with form 'request' and form 'flat': each carries only its own shape.
Call activationSpec with an unknown form: it throws, naming the known forms.
Read plugins/orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs: no spec.request, maxDepth, outputSchema or ...request; it calls activationSpec.
Read docs/HARNESS-CONTRACT.md: it names startActivation, harness-seam.mjs as the owner and the harness-seam test as the check.
expected: One input yields both activation shapes (spec.request.parent.id and spec.parent.id); form 'request' carries only the nested shape and 'flat' only the flat one; an unknown form throws an explicit refusal; the orchestrator contains none of the shape markers and calls the seam; the contract names startActivation, the seam module and the check.
failsWhen: One reader cannot see its parent on the default input, a named form carries the other shape, an unknown form silently returns a spec, the orchestrator builds the activation shape itself, or the contract stops naming the call and its owner.
trigger: A delegation is started through the seam; the two runtime readers read the same spec, a test asks for one form by name, an unknown form is requested, and the orchestrator and the contract are read as they are.
oracle: REQ-296 criteria C01 (the orchestrator carries no activation-form fields), C02 (one input, both forms; form by name; unknown form is an explicit refusal) and C03 (docs/HARNESS-CONTRACT.md lists the calls and matches the code); the two readers are the shapes named in the contract: spec.request.* for dsh 0.2.1 and the flat spec for dsh 0.2.2-rc.3.
realism: The runtime changed the activation request between the pinned versions; a kit that sends one shape breaks on the other with a runtime TypeError before a child exists. The seam is the one place that knows both shapes, and the acceptance drives it with a real delegation input (role, prompt, parent) and reads the same files the contract lists.
